messages:
Jon Park: heads up — after the continuous-batching heuristic rollout at 04:12 I'm seeing a consistent p50/p95 jump for small requests on g4-*. Throughput also dropped ~12%. Anyone already looking?
Maria Chen: noticed it on the dashboard, opening profiler now. queue depth histogram shifted right, a lot more 1-2 req microbatches. KV cache hit rate down.
Kevin O'Neill: interesting — did we change the token_budget_target or routing thresholds in that rollout?
Jon Park: yes, token_budget_target lowered to 8 for aggressive batching, and kernel-routing threshold changed from 128 -> 64 tokens as part of the new fast-path heuristics.
Sarah Li: attaching quick flame: https://redwood-internal/prof/1855004321/flame.png
Maria Chen: profiler snippet:
```
kernel_select: fast_path 62% -> 58% (expected up), slow_path 38% -> 42% (unexpected)
avg_latency_per_token_fast: 8ms
avg_latency_per_token_slow: 120ms
kv_cache_hit: 0.88 -> 0.71
microbatch_size_median: 1 -> 2
queue_wait_ms_p50: 6 -> 45
```
Maria Chen: seems like the smaller token_budget is causing more tiny microbatches that flip kernel selection to slow_path more frequently, and that in turn thrashes the KV cache (less reuse).
Kevin O'Neill: that matches a trace I pulled — most of the slow_path hits are small requests that still force model exec on the slow kernel. Kernel warmup/priming overhead kills latency.
Jon Park: shall we flip a revert flag for the heuristic while we investigate? quick rollback would confirm.
Sarah Li: I can push a roll-back gate: `rctl set feature continuous_batching_v2=false --env=prod` — takes <1m.
infra-bot: scheduled action queued: set feature continuous_batching_v2=false (user: Sarah Li)
deploy-bot: deploy started by Sarah Li — rolling out to prod clusters (g4/eu/us)
Jon Park: also let's add a short-term mitigation: bump token_budget_target to 16 instead of full revert — less aggressive but might avoid slow-path thrash. Thoughts?
Kevin O'Neill: prefer the conservative revert first to get baselines back, then we can AB test token_budget_target=12/16.
Maria Chen: agreed. I want to capture a few flamegraphs pre/post. If revert shows improvement I'll run a throughput sweep.
ops-signal-bot: paging: latency alert muted for 20m (ack by Jon Park)
deploy-bot: deploy complete — feature continuous_batching_v2=false (rollout 100%)
Maria Chen: initial numbers 2m after revert: queue_wait_ms_p50 down from 45 -> 8ms, kv_cache_hit back to 0.86, slow_path % down to 34%. throughput recovered ~10%.
Jon Park: great. We'll keep revert for now and iterate on the heuristic. Root cause summary in case notes: reducing token_budget_target to 8 increased frequency of tiny microbatches; kernel-routing threshold change (128->64) combined caused more small requests to hit slow_path. KV cache reuse dropped, amplifying latency.
Kevin O'Neill: action items:
- (Kevin) add telemetry to correlate microbatch size -> kernel_select decision (traces) — due EOD
- (Maria) run AB test with token_budget_target {12,16} + routing threshold 96 — capture p50/p95 and kv hit — start in staging tomorrow
- (Sarah) add a canary guard to not drop token_budget_target <12 for prod without explicit opt-in
- (Jon) write postmortem note and link to profiling artifacts
Sarah Li: I'll also add a short-term kernel cache prefetch for small sequences as an experiment (ttl 50ms) to reduce KV cold misses.
Maria Chen: adding profiling links: full flame + traces + kv metrics: https://redwood-internal/prof/1855004321/full-report.pdf
Jon Park: thanks all — keeping revert live until AB results. I'll update the incident channel with numbers. :thumbsup:
Kevin O'Neill: small clarifying note — this isn't a model perf regression, it's an orchestration/heuristic regression (kernel routing + batching). important to capture in postmortem.
Jon Park: agreed. tagging for postmortem writeup.
Maria Chen: will upload the E2E trace bundle to the incident doc in 15m.
Sarah Li: reopening the feature flag gating PR to add minimum token_budget_target enforcement.
Jon Park: closing loop — p50 back to baseline after revert, ops signal stable. Will follow up with AB plan.
